description: This woodland walk explores Woodlawn Woods near Ballinasloe in County Galway. You begin at the car park near Woodlawn railway station, where an entrance leads directly into the surrounding woodland. The initial section of the walk passes through managed forestry, with rows of spruce and larch forming long shaded avenues. The paths are mostly soft underfoot, a mix of soil and gravel, with occasional roots and shallow channels where water has run off after rain. As you move further into the woods the character changes, with patches of mixed native trees such as oak, birch, alder and ash. These areas feel more open and natural, with glimpses of birds in the branches and, if you are quiet, the chance of seeing deer in the distance. In spring and summer the undergrowth is dotted with wildflowers like foxglove and wood sorrel, while later in the year ferns and moss dominate the shaded ground. There are waymarked nature trails with signs and boards that describe the wildlife and plants to look out for. The atmosphere is peaceful, with the sound of wind moving through the canopy and the scent of damp moss and fallen leaves creating a strong woodland feel. Deeper in the walk the trees thin and the estate comes into view. Woodlawn House, a large Italianate mansion built in the eighteenth century and later expanded, stands as the centrepiece. From the paths you catch sight of its tall roofline and chimneys above the trees. Around it are the remnants of estate buildings including old lodges, walled gardens and service houses that hint at the former grandeur of the estate. Some trails skirt water features and small boggy hollows, adding variety to the route. Streams and pools appear in clearings, reflecting the light between the trees. Following the paths in a loop brings you gradually back towards the station, with one last view of the house framed through the woodland before the track leads back into the shelter of the forest. You can continue your woodland walking in the area on the Mountbellew Forest Walk .
